_readme: Events and Multimedia Production, Version 1.5: the page's words and its media configuration, section by section (src/pages/work/events-video.astro and src/components/events/). Copy follows John's Combined Build Brief and the V1.1, V1.2, V1.3, V1.4 and V1.5 delta briefs (October 16, 2026) and the facts in his working log; no metric is published until it has been verified, and nothing here mentions an unannounced pilot, contract or Foundation discussions, investor diligence, data rooms or fundraising. Media slots name asset ids in src/data/assets.json: to replace a placeholder, drop the file in and approve its entry there; the layout never changes, because every slot already holds its final aspect ratio. Unapproved slots show a labeled placeholder in `npm run dev` only and nothing in a production build.

hero._hero: One editorial reel (V1.2), in place of V1.1's three programs and their control: the chapters below, in this order, each one video cut from the brief's ranges (assets.json has each chapter's ranges and edits), played through once and crossfaded (350ms) into the next, round and round, muted. The label at the top left of the frame reads the chapter's number and title, numbered in order among the chapters whose video is approved and present: the team interview's chapter is pending, so it is left out entirely (no placeholder) and the chapters after it carry the lower numbers until its video is added. `pos` places the crop of the wide cinematic frame on each video (object-position), chosen so the burned-in captions stay whole and clear of the rail, and heads stay in, at both of the frame's proportions (2.2:1, and 2.4:1 on shorter wide screens); `fitNarrow` is how the video fills the 16:9 frame on narrow screens.
hero.headline: From live experience to lasting momentum.
hero.copy: I turn live opportunities into complete marketing systems, from sponsorship and on-site production to content, distribution, and the relationships that continue after the room clears.

monitor._monitor: V1.4, the program monitor's few words: beside the label at the top left a steady tally dot (lit while the reel plays) and `program`, so it reads PROGRAM · 01 / LIVE PRESENTATION; `timecode` before the running counter at the top right (TC 00:00:04:22). On the smallest frames the counter steps aside first, then the word.

transition._transition: Replaces the run of show (V1.1): the five stages as one phrase, revealed word by word over about seven tenths of a screen of scrolling, held, then straight into the activation. On small screens it breaks into two lines after `break` words.

activation.headline: The work starts before anyone enters the room.
activation.copy: Before the doors open, I negotiate sponsorships and pricing, coordinate with event hosts, source and price merchandise, and work with design on screen animations and physical assets. I plan how those pieces come together on site and how the activation continues through content and distribution afterward.
activation._visual: An original 3D render of the activation (V1.1, replacing the schematic; since V1.3 a concept rendering combining the activation elements John plans and coordinates across events, tied to no one event or booth, as the paragraph and the caption say): an illustrative composite, not a photograph, made for this page in Blender (scripts/render/; the spatial and lighting reference is reference/events-video/booth-render.png, never published). The television and the projected wall play their loops while the frame is in view; reduced motion, a data-saving preference, a small screen or no JavaScript keep the render with both screens on their poster frames.
activation.caption: Concept rendering combining the activation elements I plan and coordinate across events.

deck._deck: 04 The Expanding Production Deck (V1.3, deployed from the V1.2 review checkpoint; V1.4 made it one vertical accordion at every width; V1.5 gave its words room and new copy): the live presentation, the production room and the event film in one stack, every chapter's header always visible and one chapter open at a time (the live presentation to begin with), opened by a click, a tap or the keyboard; nothing advances by itself. An open chapter holds its media and its words side by side on wide screens (the media about 58% of the two columns), stacked on narrow ones. Its words: the headline, the introduction, up to three things John did, the outcome, and the fine-print credit (`credit`, with `participants` as a second line where a chapter has them); on wide screens the words use the column's full height, the headline near its top and the credit toward its bottom. Its media: a muted preview (an approved loop of 8 to 15 seconds that plays only while it is shown and in view, with its own pause control) and, where a chapter has `full`, the film itself, which `watch` plays in place with sound and its controls. Since V1.5 the live presentation has no full film, only its preview. The production room opens on its setup photograph (setupFinal below).

chapters.label: Live presentation
chapters.headline: From live presentation to lasting content.
chapters.context: I led Bolt Liquidity’s Sui Summit presentation from early planning through session strategy, deck direction, live production, capture, and post-event distribution.
points: Secured the slot, helped shape the subject, and promoted the session
Directed the deck, presentation setup, and live slides
Captured the presentation from multiple angles and repackaged it for continued distribution
chapters.outcome: Event-led relationships contribute to ongoing conversations and integrations with key ecosystem partners.
chapters.credit: Organized, directed, and captured by John Cowin · Speaker Max McKendry · Deck design Bob van der Meer

chapters.label: Production room
chapters.headline: Build the set. Direct the take. Shape the final cut.
chapters.context: At ETHDenver, I turned a production room and a minimal kit into a repeatable technical explainer series.
points: Built a compact setup with two cameras and a clip-on mic
Wrote 20 interview questions and directed multiple takes
Selected the strongest moments and shaped the edit direction
chapters.outcome: One focused production session became a library of finished product explainers for the YouTube channel and social media.
chapters.credit: Concept, questions, direction, capture, and edit briefs by John Cowin · On-camera Max McKendry · Final edit Bob van der Meer

chapters.label: Event film
chapters.headline: Capture the event. Connect the ecosystem.
chapters.context: At Sui Fest, I developed an interview-led event film featuring established teams across the ecosystem and positioned Bolt alongside them as an active participant. I conducted the interviews, coordinated contributors, shaped the edit, and led content distribution.
points: Interviewed established ecosystem teams and included Bolt within the same editorial frame
Built the narrative around a shared event experience rather than a standalone brand feature
Tagged participating teams and coordinated distribution to extend the film’s reach
chapters.outcome: Featuring multiple teams turned the film into a shared distribution asset, expanding Bolt’s presence across the ecosystem.
chapters.credit: Concept, interviews, coordination, and distribution by John Cowin · Final edit Bob van der Meer
chapters.participants: With Cetus, Bluefin, 7K DeFi, NAVI & Astros, FlowX Finance, DoubleUp, Claynosaurz and Talus

setupFinal._setupFinal: V1.4: the production room's Setup and Final, inside its chapter of the deck; V1.5 made the switch a clear segmented control. Two equal options, SETUP and FINAL, just above the stage, the selected one filled in the page's accent. Setup, the default, shows the behind-the-scenes photograph (since V1.5 without a caption); Final crossfades, within the same stage, to the finished explainer (the chapter's muted preview with its pause control), and only under Final does Watch full video with sound show (its line is kept under Setup, so nothing below moves). The reader makes the switch; nothing changes by itself, the stage keeps its size, and with reduced motion the change is immediate. Never side by side. `label` names the control for assistive technology.
setupFinal.label: Setup and final

conclusion._conclusion: V1.2: the conclusion and the former Amplify section (Every event opens a longer conversation.) in one closing: the static row of the five stages as a quiet callback (never animated a second time), the headline, one paragraph, then the way on to the next case study in order, Creator Campaigns (the collection wraps around), then Contact.
conclusion.headline: The room clears. The work keeps moving.
conclusion.copy: An event is only the starting point. I turn live moments into content, extend their reach through partner and ecosystem distribution, and carry that momentum into strategic relationships and new opportunities.
conclusion.nextLine: Next, see how I build creator partnerships into campaigns designed to travel.
